findings.title: remove_member passes an integer to the has_many collection delete
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` is given an integer id. Depending on the Rails version, `CollectionProxy#delete` with an id may not remove the join row correctly, or it may raise `AssociationTypeMismatch`. The spec only covers the happy path through the controller. It is safer to load the user (`User.find`) or use `delete_all`/`where` on the join table, and to return a proper error when the user is not a member.

findings.title: Unbounded and unvalidated limit/offset on public members endpoint
findings.body: `limit` comes straight from `params[:limit].to_i` with no upper cap, and negative values are not rejected. A client can request an arbitrarily large page, which removes the old protection and is a DoS risk. A negative offset or limit can also cause a database error. Clamp the values, for example `limit` to 1..200 and `offset` to >= 0.

findings.title: Response format change breaks existing consumers of /groups/:name/members
findings.body: The endpoint used to return a bare array of users and now returns `{members, meta}`. Any other client or plugin using the old shape will break. The old default of 200 users for automatic groups also changed to 50 for every group. Only the group members view was updated to the new shape.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives one extra, empty page when the count divides evenly. For 50 users with a limit of 50 it reports 2 pages. The next button then navigates to an empty page. Use `Math.ceil`.

findings.title: addMembers never clears the usernames input and ignores failures
findings.body: After a successful add, `usernames` stays populated (the code has a TODO acknowledging this). A repeated click re-submits the same names. There is no error handling if the PUT fails, so the user gets no feedback.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined for an unnamed group
findings.body: The old code returned a resolved promise. Now it returns `undefined`, so any caller that chains `.then` on it will throw.
